narratives.Overview:
## Recut (post-bind, 2026-09-07)

Operator recut after accepted synthesis [5574304813](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4240#issuecomment-5574304813) / successor lean [5574299098](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4240#issuecomment-5574299098).

Locked: a bound behavioral or negative clause with no extractable tokens and no green executable run still blocks `scope:complete`. Do not restore `verified.length > 0` as a set predicate.

Dropped from this recut:

- Defect 1 (the walk prints `verify:ac passed` on fail) -- already `#3497` `labelVerdict`.
- Defect 2 (apostrophe and quote as one delimiter class) -- already `#4103` quote-class pairing.

Census only, not this recut: expected tokens still cannot contain quotes.

The older completed-arc record does not clear this recut body.

Companion #4239 is a different component (CLI help for `scope:complete`) and is not this target.

## Problem

`scope:complete` still cannot finish an honest stated-rung brief whose criteria are all behavioral or negative, once those clauses are bound to a real declared artifact.

At pin `7236655ef6f586169c94f3c4ce5eeccf5668960b`:

- `walkOne` on a declared path with no extractable tokens and no `EXISTENCE_CLAIM` returns `unverifiable` with `adjudicable: true`.
- `countUnverifiedAdjudicableClauses` counts that row.
- `clauseWalkBlocks` then blocks unless `hasGreenExecutableRun`.
- `#3334` still refuses an empty `clauses[]`, so deleting the set is not a way through.
- There is no clause-level non-file evidence kind (`#3240` `x-directive/evidence` is a plan-item shape, not a clause shape).

The original `verified.length > 0 || walked.length === 0` bar is gone (`#3826` / `#3835`). Unbound clauses are not adjudicable and do not block. A green executable run already excuses unverifiable adjudicable clauses. The remaining hole is narrower and still real: **clauses-only, bound, behavioral or negative, no executable run**.

The pressure is the same as the original filing: mint a grep-able token chosen for checkability, or add an executable command, even when the meaningful criterion is "callers are unchanged" / "no canary glob was added".

## Residual (next-build)

1. A stated-rung brief whose only clauses are bound behavioral or negative (no extractable tokens, no existence claim) and that has no executable commands must be able to complete without minting a grep token, **or** the refusal must name this case instead of looking like a failed walk.
2. Unbound (non-adjudicable) clauses stay non-blocking.
3. A green executable run still excuses unverifiable adjudicable clauses (`clauseWalkBlocks`).
4. Do not restore `verified.length > 0` as a set predicate.
5. `#3334` empty `clauses[]` still refuses.

## Open fork

Give clauses an explicit non-file evidence kind (as `#3240` plan items already can), or treat a bound behavioral clause like an unbound one (no oracle, so `failed === 0` is the strongest static verdict). Remedy is not locked.

## Non-goals

- Re-landing `#3497` or `#4103`.
- Changing quote-class pairing, or adding backtick expected-token delimiters, unless a later recut asks for quoted-value tokens.
- Companion #4239.

## Acceptance (draft)

- [ ] A fixture with one bound behavioral clause, no extractable tokens, no executable commands, and a declared `file_scope` path does not fail `scope:complete` / `verify:ac` solely because the walk returned `unverifiable`, **or** the printed verdict names that case.
- [ ] The same fixture with a green executable run still does not block on that unverifiable clause.
- [ ] An unbound clause still does not block.
- [ ] Empty `clauses[]` still fails `#3334`.
- [ ] Tests pin the residual; they do not re-assert the old `verified.length > 0` set predicate.

## History (original filing)

The body below is the 0.104.0 three-defect write-up as filed. It is history. It is not the next-build contract.

---

## Summary

Three defects in the `#3323` clause walk on `@deftai/directive-core@0.104.0`, found while binding acceptance clauses to clear the `#3357` precondition on `scope:complete`. All three are reproducible with a two-clause fixture and no project state.

Companion to #4239 (same session, different component: that one is the CLI help for `scope:complete`, this one is `verify-ac/clauses.js`).

## 1. The walk prints `verify:ac passed` when it failed

The line is emitted identically whether the walk passed or failed. Only the counts and the exit code carry the signal — and the `#3357` refusal on `scope:complete` embeds this same misleading line in its own output, so a refusal reads as a pass.

| Fixture | Walk result | Printed | Exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| one verified clause | `1 verified, 0 unverifiable, 0 failed` | `verify:ac passed (#3284) [rung=stated]` | 0 |
| one failed clause | `0 verified, 0 unverifiable, 1 failed` | `verify:ac passed (#3284) [rung=stated]` | **1** |
| one unverifiable clause | `0 verified, 1 unverifiable, 0 failed` | `verify:ac passed (#3284) [rung=stated]` | **1** |

This matters because the documented remediation for `#3357` is *"Run `task verify:ac -- <completing-xbrief>` and stamp executable plan.acceptance"* — and running exactly that prints `passed`. Every path a user is pointed at tells them the thing that is blocking them is fine.

## 2. An apostrophe in clause prose is parsed as a token delimiter

`extractExpectedTokens` (`dist/verify-ac/clauses.js:305`):

```js
const quoted = /["']([^"'\n]{3,80})["']/g;
```

Straight quotes and apostrophes are the same character class, so ordinary English possessives split a junk "expected token" out of otherwise-correct text and fail the clause. Repro:

```json
{ "id": 1,
  "text": "The doc describes the project's own posture ('AgentSentri').",
  "artifact_path": "README.md" }
```

```
verify:ac clause walk (#3323): 0 verified, 0 unverifiable, 1 failed
  [failed] clause 1 @ README.md: The doc describes the project's own posture ('AgentSentri').
           — expected token(s) missing from README.md: s own posture (
```

`AgentSentri` is present in `README.md` ten times. The clause fails on `s own posture (` — text between the apostrophe in `project's` and the opening quote of the real token. Removing the apostrophe makes the identical clause pass. This hit real briefs twice in one session ("the skill's own Zod schema", "another project's MCP resource"), and the failure names a token the author never wrote, so it reads as a checker bug rather than a prose problem.

## 3. Some real criteria cannot be expressed as tokens, which blocks completion

Same character class means a token can never contain a quote, so a criterion about a quoted value is unexpressible: `"jsx": "preserve"` cannot be a token. `looksLikeFilePath` (line 34) additionally drops path-shaped tokens silently. A clause left with zero usable tokens falls through to `unverifiable`, and:

```js
const ok = failed.length === 0 && (verified.length > 0 || walked.length === 0);  // line 453
```

`scope:complete` requires that `ok`, so **at least one clause must be `verified`**. A brief whose stated criteria are all behavioral or negative ("no canary include glob was added", "existing callers are unchanged") can never satisfy it. Two briefs in this session were `0 verified, N unverifiable` with hand-authored `rung=stated` clauses that were *accurate*; the only way through was to bind one clause each to a token in a real file — chosen for checkability, not because it was the most meaningful criterion. The gate rewards clauses that are easy to grep for over clauses that describe the delivery.

(For the record, deleting the clause set is *not* a shortcut: `#3334 soft_empty` catches an empty `clauses[]` at exit 1. The pressure is toward weak clauses, not no clauses.)

## Repro

```bash
cat > /tmp/repro-apostrophe.xbrief.json <<'EOF'
{
  "xBRIEFInfo": {"version": "0.8", "author": "repro", "description": "repro",
                 "created": "2026-09-07T00:00:00Z", "updated": "2026-09-07T00:00:00Z"},
  "plan": {"title": "repro apostrophe token", "status": "running", "items": [],
    "acceptance": {"commands": [], "none_stated": true, "source_rung": "stated",
      "clauses": [{"id": 1,
        "text": "The doc describes the project's own posture ('AgentSentri').",
        "artifact_path": "README.md"}]}}
}
EOF
deft verify:ac --xbrief /tmp/repro-apostrophe.xbrief.json; echo "exit=$?"
```

Run from any project whose `README.md` contains `AgentSentri` (or swap the token). Drop the `'AgentSentri'` token for fixture 3; drop the apostrophe for the passing control.

## Suggested fix

1. Print `verify:ac failed` (or nothing) when the walk is not ok — never `passed` on exit 1. This one is a one-line change and removes most of the confusion on its own.
2. Use a token delimiter that cannot collide with prose: backticks, or paired straight double quotes only, and ignore unpaired apostrophes.
3. Let a token be delimited so it can contain quotes (backticks would do both jobs).
4. Reconsider `verified.length > 0` as the completion bar, or give clauses an explicit non-file evidence kind so a behavioral criterion can carry `x-directive/evidence` (as `#3240` plan items already can) instead of being forced into a grep. As written, an honest all-behavioral clause set cannot complete.

## Environment

- `@deftai/directive` global CLI, engine `@deftai/directive-core@0.104.0`
- macOS (darwin 25.5.0), Node via global npm install
- Consumer project (`deftai/agentsentri`) with a vendored content-only `.deft/core` deposit
